title: OpenAPI 3.1 and YAML Support in .NET 10
description: Learn how .NET 10 adds OpenAPI 3.1 schema support and enables YAML output for API documentation.

data.text: .NET 10 brings full support for the OpenAPI 3.1 specification and the ability to generate YAML-formatted API documentation alongside JSON. OpenAPI 3.1 aligns more closely with JSON Schema draft 2020-12, offering improved type definitions and nullable handling that better represent modern API contracts.

You can now configure your ASP.NET Core project to emit the OpenAPI document in YAML format. YAML is often preferred for human readability and is widely used in API design tools like Stoplight and Swagger Editor.

data.title: Configure YAML OpenAPI output in Program.cs
data.content: Enable YAML output for the Swagger/OpenAPI document in .NET 10

data.text: OpenAPI 3.1 brings several improvements that are especially useful for .NET 10 developers. Nullable reference types now map cleanly to the nullable property in JSON Schema. The oneOf, anyOf, and allOf keywords behave consistently with JSON Schema, and the discriminator object supports polymorphic schemas more elegantly.

data.title: Why OpenAPI 3.1 Matters
data.text: OpenAPI 3.1 resolves ambiguities present in 3.0, particularly around nullable types and schema composition. If you generate client SDKs from your OpenAPI document, upgrading to 3.1 can produce more accurate type definitions.

If you need to produce a YAML file at build or publish time, you can use the OpenAPI document processor to serialize the document as YAML. This is useful for CI/CD pipelines that distribute API specs to downstream consumers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: .NET 10 supports OpenAPI 3.1, aligning with the latest JSON Schema draft.
YAML output is supported out of the box for human-readable API specs.
Nullable reference types map correctly to OpenAPI 3.1 schemas.
Use PreSerializeFilters to customize the generated document before it is served.

data.title: Summary
points: OpenAPI 3.1 is the default document version in .NET 10.
Enable YAML output via SwaggerUI configuration.
Use the document filters to customize servers, tags, and schemas.
YAML output improves collaboration with frontend and QA teams.
data.takeaway: OpenAPI 3.1 with YAML support makes .NET 10 APIs easier to document, consume, and collaborate on across teams.
